Render-node headless compositor backend

Status: accepted, 2026-10-20.

compd has three backends: kms-live owns physical scanout, nested draws inside a host compositor, and headless draws a virtual output using only a render node. Headless is the offscreen test and future recording target; hardware behaviour continues to be tested on KMS.

The headless backend lives beside nested at compd layer 4. GBM/EGL opens the selected render node and verifies the EGL device identity. There is no DRM device, master, connector, libseat, udev or libinput. The virtual output is headless-0; mode and scale are explicit. Two offscreen GLES textures alternate, with full repaints after scene damage. A one-shot software timer caps frames at 60 Hz and stops while idle. Software presentation uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC and claims no hardware completion or vblank. COMPD_HEADLESS_REFRESH_HZ may select a lower rate from 30 through 60 Hz; the virtual mode and frame timer use the same rate. The default is 60 Hz.

The binding profile is headless; the default Bus service is comp-headless, with comp-<name> available through --bus-service for instances. Headless never requests realtime priority or negative nice, starts no XWayland, and leaves the desktop session environment alone.

Headless owns agent input authority without a VT; session locks still clear agent input, while KMS and nested retain their session-pause rules. seat0 is advertised with no capabilities, and human input refuses seat_unavailable. The agent pointer starts at output centre; absolute headless-0 moves clamp to the mode's logical bounds. Each Bus service has its own observation topics, window registry and presentation statistics.

Screencopy and Bus captures run after completed offscreen rendering, including on idle outputs. The normal picture excludes cursor elements; a second pass is made only when a capture requests them. Cursor inclusion is chosen per capture, including mixed requests in one frame, and an unavailable picture fails its capture rather than substituting another cursor policy. Capturing unchanged content does not count as a new presentation.

Deployment and recording

An instance is a headless desk: its own nspawn machine, noded, session bus, PipeWire and portald, with only the GPU render node bound and no VT, tty or seatd. compd-headless@.service uses the session slot %i, just as compd@ does: a console desk uses a VT number; a headless desk can use rec. Both read /etc/mixos/session/%i.env. Inside the desk, the compositor's Bus service is comp; each desk has its own node. The standalone CLI default remains comp-headless.

The component owns mixos-headless.slice with CPUQuota=200%; the desk's compositor runs there at nice 10. Desk provisioning places its portal, PipeWire, WirePlumber and encoder in that slice too. The container has its own quota, so the slice does not need a per-instance name. COMPD_HEADLESS_REFRESH_HZ passes through the session environment file.

portald's serve --screencast-max-framerate N sets the cast ceiling in 1..=120 Hz. It defaults to 30, preserving console sessions; a headless desk can request 60 through its portal unit drop-in. This ceiling does not change the compositor's refresh rate. These templates do not provision or start a desk.

Phase 4b acceptance measures presentation cadence: presented_hz is the presented-frame count divided by the paced probe's elapsed time, and cadence_missed counts presentation gaps greater than 1.5 requested intervals. Captured-frame uniqueness is measured from the probe's pixel frame IDs. The client-deadline missed count remains a regression guard only: two free-running 60 Hz clocks beat against that deadline without establishing a compositor cadence defect.

The Phase 2 plain Wayland EGL client probe (weston-simple-egl, with WAYLAND_DEBUG=client) created its first wl_buffer through wl_shm_pool. Its rendered pixels survived composition and screencopy, but this was a wl_shm fallback. Client DMA-BUF negotiation remains unproven; this probe does not establish the GPU-client DMA-BUF path.

Phase 5 uses ced's real egui/wgpu window with a private noded and editd, so ced.state {text:true} can confirm agent-seat typing independently of pixels. The reference helper services/compd/crates/testkit/scripts/app_reference.mix creates a fresh document and places an 800×560 window at (80,60), scale 1, in either session; the console-desk reference is captured separately with that same helper. Before the first GPU run, the acceptance threshold is fixed at grayscale SSIM ≥ 0.99 for repeated idle captures and the console/headless comparison, allowing minor rasterisation differences while rejecting material layout changes. The known typed line must produce SSIM < 0.999 against the blank document, alongside exact Bus text readback. SSIM uses uniform sliding 8×8 valid windows, population covariance, Rec.601 luma, K1=0.01, K2=0.03 and L=255. A test-only ced launcher installs a log subscriber around the unchanged entry point to record the chosen wgpu adapter; Wayland client tracing records the actual buffer creation request. A shm result is reported as a weaker client-buffer claim, even when wgpu renders on a GPU. Software wgpu adapters are recorded explicitly and establish no GPU-client claim.

What the headless-only run proves, and does not (review, 2026-10-21): with no console reference supplied, the test shows a large, stable rendered change after typing plus exact model text; it does not check glyph correctness (tofu or a wrong font fallback would still pass). Glyphs are only pinned by the console comparison. SSIM at 0.99 tolerates uniform brightness drift: a +10 luma shift scores about 0.9955 at mid grey and 0.9988 at bright grey, so a brightness regression is within the threshold by design and must be caught elsewhere. The tested artefact is the test-only launcher, which compiles the shipped entry point from the same source; drift is a compile error, never silent. The first run chose a software Vulkan adapter (llvmpipe) with wl_shm: forcing a hardware wgpu adapter on the render node is an open follow-up, as are the test's fixed post-typing sleep (retry once on an unchanged capture), the helper's leftover .session directory on failure, and its reliance on spawn merging the parent environment.
